note: FICTIONAL rows in the archive's documented format. expected_later gives the deterministic classifier label for each later-dated row (line numbers are 1-based within the case).

cases.name: ptbnl_formally_named
cases.explains: a placeholder row exists in the same direction and exactly one later player follows: a formal PTBNL resolution (migration 028 already models it; it is NOT an addition)
cases.canonical: ptbnl_resolutions row on the SEA>LAD placeholder asset; no trade_asset_additions row

cases.name: added_later_unstated
cases.explains: a player row under the trade id dated later with no placeholder: the source does not say why; kept as an addition, never called a PTBNL
cases.canonical: trade_asset_additions row, addition_kind ADDED_LATER_UNSTATED, added_on 2030-07-20 on the SEA>LAD package

cases.name: added_to_trade_by_source
cases.explains: the source types the later row Tp (added to a trade, usually because an original player refused to report or retired): an amendment-like addition stated by the source

cases.name: ambiguous_placeholders
cases.explains: two placeholders in one direction and one later player: which PTBNL was named is not stated, so a person decides; nothing is paired automatically
cases.canonical: none until a person pairs it (then a ptbnl_resolutions row)

cases.name: later_cash_row
cases.explains: a later row with no player is a cash or text row, not a player
cases.canonical: held: cash of unknown amount added later has no representation without an amendment/asset effective date

cases.name: later_void
cases.explains: a later void row is an amendment of the whole transaction

cases.name: ids_reused_across_unrelated_rows
cases.explains: a repeated id on non-trade rows is not a trade group: no later member, nothing merged
